name: CA-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 8-point Democratic lean plus a favorable national environment
Harder's massive financial advantage ($4.7M cash vs. under $20K)
Prediction markets price Harder at 97-98% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point to a Safe D race: an 8-point Democratic district, a strong Democratic environment, and Harder's overwhelming cash advantage of roughly $4.7 million against McBride's $19,000. Markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price Harder near 97-98%, consistent with a double-digit expected margin.
model.watch: Any late surge in Republican outside spending or polling showing McBride within single digits would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Josh Harder, the Democratic incumbent, is heavily favored to win a fourth term in this Central Valley district that leans Democratic by about eight points. He has raised over $4 million and holds a cash advantage of more than $4.7 million, while Republican John McBride has raised only about $52,000. No outside groups have meaningfully engaged on either side, and no public polls of the race are available.

Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price Harder's chances at 97 to 98 percent, and the underlying fundamentals — district lean, a favorable environment for Democrats, incumbency, and the money gap — all point the same direction. The main uncertainty is simply the absence of polling, which keeps the margin estimate somewhat loose but does not change the expected outcome.
